topics.title: Custom Properties, calc() & Design Tokens
topics.summary: Create reusable values that participate in the cascade and can be overridden per component, theme, or state.

concepts.name: Custom properties
concepts.explanation: Names beginning with -- store token-like values. var(--name, fallback) reads them at computed-value time and can provide a fallback.

concepts.name: Cascade-powered theming
concepts.explanation: Because custom properties inherit and cascade, changing a token on an ancestor can theme an entire subtree without rewriting every component rule.

concepts.name: Derived values
concepts.explanation: Combine tokens with calc(), min(), max(), clamp(), and color functions to derive component values instead of duplicating constants.

topics.challenge: Define at least three custom properties and use them in a component, including one calc() or color-mix() expression.
topics.hint: Put global defaults on :root, then override tokens closer to a component when you need a local theme.

topics.title: Advanced Selectors & Relational Styling
topics.summary: Use attribute selectors, combinators, structural pseudo-classes, :is(), :where(), :not(), and :has() while keeping selector intent readable.

concepts.name: Functional pseudo-classes
concepts.explanation: :is() groups selector alternatives, :where() does the same with zero specificity, and :not() excludes matches.

concepts.name: Relational selection
concepts.explanation: :has() can style an element based on matching descendants or relative selectors, enabling parent-like conditions that previously needed JavaScript.

concepts.name: Selector cost is secondary
concepts.explanation: Modern engines handle selectors well; prioritize maintainability, scope, and predictable specificity before micro-optimizing selector speed.

topics.challenge: Write one :has() rule and one grouped rule using :is() or :where().
topics.hint: :where() is especially useful when you want matching power without adding specificity.

topics.title: Keyframe Animation & Motion Systems
topics.summary: Build multi-stage animations, compose timing and fill behavior, and provide reduced-motion alternatives.

concepts.name: Keyframes
concepts.explanation: @keyframes defines intermediate states. animation-name, duration, timing-function, iteration-count, direction, and fill-mode control playback.

concepts.name: Composable motion
concepts.explanation: Animate transform and opacity where possible for smooth visual feedback, and avoid motion that changes layout every frame unless necessary.

concepts.name: Reduced motion
concepts.explanation: Use prefers-reduced-motion to remove or simplify nonessential animations. The goal is not always “zero motion”; it is avoiding harmful or distracting motion.

topics.challenge: Create a keyframe animation with at least three stages and disable it for reduced-motion users.
topics.hint: Separate the @keyframes definition from the element that applies the animation.

topics.title: Intrinsic Sizing & Content-Driven Layout
topics.summary: Use min-content, max-content, fit-content(), minmax(), aspect-ratio, and overflow-aware sizing to let content participate in layout decisions.

concepts.name: Intrinsic keywords
concepts.explanation: min-content represents the smallest width without avoidable overflow, while max-content represents the unwrapped preferred width.

concepts.name: fit-content
concepts.explanation: fit-content() grows toward the ideal size but respects an available-space limit, useful for labels, sidebars, and content-sized tracks.

concepts.name: Aspect ratio
concepts.explanation: aspect-ratio reserves proportional space and helps components remain stable before media loads.

topics.challenge: Build a two-column grid where the sidebar has content-aware sizing and the main area can shrink safely.
topics.hint: minmax(0, 1fr) is useful when long content would otherwise force a grid track wider than expected.

topics.title: Component CSS Architecture
topics.summary: Organize selectors, tokens, variants, state, and layout responsibilities so components remain reusable and predictable as a project grows.

concepts.name: Separate responsibilities
concepts.explanation: Page layout rules should not quietly depend on deep component internals. Give components explicit classes and modifiers for their public styling contract.

concepts.name: Low specificity
concepts.explanation: Class-based selectors, :where(), and thoughtful nesting make overrides easier than long descendant chains or frequent !important.

concepts.name: State naming
concepts.explanation: Use clear state hooks such as [aria-current="page"], .is-active, or data-state rather than styling by incidental DOM position when state is semantic.

topics.challenge: Create a component class, one variant, one state selector, and one element/subpart selector.
topics.hint: Treat classes and data attributes as an API: a future developer should understand why each selector exists.
